$comment: Platform context projection, contract 1.10.0 (ADR 0028). Compare filesystem-store.schema.json: THAT verb may write anywhere in the workspace EXCEPT .cliora/, and this one may write ONLY under .cliora/{context,process,reference}/ - the two writable sets are disjoint, and neither replaces a byte. The path pattern is the enforcement, not a comment: a destination outside those three subtrees, a traversal segment, or .cliora/uploads (the user's image-drop area) and .cliora/.gitignore (which the user may own) are unrepresentable rather than merely refused. Still absent, and enforced by additionalProperties:false: overwrite, mode beyond the single allowed value, precondition. Nothing in this payload can ask to replace something.

process_version.$comment: The content version of the process definition. It becomes a directory name, so it is bounded and free of separators.

files.$comment: At most 32. A context pack is one file, a credential is one file, and the process notes are a handful; a projection that needed more than this would be projecting something it should be pointing at (D8).

path.$comment: Workspace-relative and confined to the three platform-owned subtrees. The negative lookahead refuses a `..` segment anywhere, the same construction filesystem-store uses: containment has to be unrepresentable rather than merely checked. `uploads` and `.gitignore` under .cliora/ belong to the user-facing write path and are outside this pattern by construction.

mode.$comment: One legal value. The field exists so a future 0700 does not need a schema change; today anything else is refused on the wire.

data.$comment: Canonical standard-alphabet base64, capped at the base64 length of 64 KiB. Far below filesystem.store's ceiling on purpose: the context pack's budget is 4 KB (D8), and a projection large enough to need more is one that should be giving the agent a path instead of a payload. minLength 0 accepts an empty file.
